summary_plain: Moves about 36 arcseconds per hour across 30 images over 21.3 hours. Not yet checked against JPL's catalog of known asteroids and comets.

source.processing_note: Zodiacal light model (ZODI) and residual background (2-D plus per-row) subtracted; pixels SPHEREx flags as unusable, and detector-edge rows with raised noise from edge glow, are filled from their neighbors (or set to the sky level) for display only and only inside the detector, while measurements use the masked data; pixels outside the detector are transparent; fixed asinh stretch shared by all images of the field; 64 x 64 px stamp at 6.15 arcsec/px centered on the detection

orbit.reported_orbit: The arc is too short to fix one orbit, so this is the most circular of the 190 sampled orbits that fit the detections; the clones show the range.

known_object.not_checked_reason: JPL Horizons did not answer for 1426 Riviera (1937 GF), the closest known object (about 23″ away in JPL's quick search).

scores.definition: Rule-based ranking score in [0, 1]: motion_consistency x snr x (1 - artifact_likelihood). It orders candidates for review. It is not a probability.

history.change: linked 30 detections over 4 visits from 2025-06-22 to 2025-06-22

disclaimer: An unmatched candidate may be an imaging artifact, a measurement error, or an object missing from the catalogs we checked. This is not a discovery claim.
